repo_notes.content: Jekyll plugin (Ruby >= 3.3) that generates .br/.zst/.gz siblings next to text assets via a :site, :post_write dispatcher (priority defaults to 10; compress_flow.priority supports 0..10), so precompressed-capable static servers serve them with zero per-request CPU.
Design: shells out to the platform brotli/zstd/gzip CLIs rather than native Ruby bindings — no native-extension dependency risk, best available quality levels.
Production-only by default: enabled resolves to Jekyll.env == 'production' unless compress_flow.enabled is set explicitly in _config.yml.
Missing compressor binary aborts once per format (fail_on_error: false downgrades to warning) — never silently ships uncompressed output.
Specs create real tmpdir sites and shell out to the real compressor CLIs; brotli/zstd/gzip must be installed to run them (CI installs them via apt).
Quality gate: bundle exec rake runs rubocop + markdownlint + bundler-audit + rspec + gem build.
See AGENTS.md for full project context and conventions.
